questions.scenario: You are playing a futuristic sci-fi video game. What is your favorite part?

options.text: Exploring endless galaxies, mapping star systems, and discovering new planets.
Using weird abilities like teleportation, phasing through walls, or time manipulation.
Building massive energy reactors, upgrading laser weapons, and testing out heavy machinery.
Figuring out the hidden rules, cheat codes, and the underlying logic of the game's universe.

questions.scenario: You are looking up at a perfectly clear night sky. What goes through your mind?

options.text: I try to identify constellations and wonder what happens inside a black hole.
I wonder if the starlight hitting my eye is acting as a particle or a wave right now.
I wish I had a high-tech, massive telescope so I could measure the exact spectrum of that light.
I think about the mathematical equations of gravity that are silently holding everything together.

questions.scenario: You have to choose a major project for the school science fair. What do you build?

options.text: A detailed model of the solar system showing the exact orbital paths of the planets.
A presentation on levitating magnets using extremely cold superconductors.
A working 'cloud chamber' that actually lets you see background radiation trails with your own eyes.
A deep, mind-bending presentation explaining the concept of the fourth dimension or time travel.

questions.scenario: You are watching a sci-fi superhero movie (like Ant-Man or Interstellar). What grabs your attention?

options.text: The realistic depiction of wormholes, time dilation, and the massive scale of space.
The scenes where they shrink down to the 'quantum realm' where the normal rules of physics break.
The cool laboratory scenes where they physically build the high-tech suits and giant machines.
Pausing the movie to see if the complex math on the genius scientist's chalkboard actually makes sense.

questions.scenario: When faced with a really difficult puzzle or brain teaser, how do you handle it?

options.text: I zoom out to look at the 'big picture' to see how all the major pieces connect.
I look for weird, paradoxical, or out-of-the-box solutions that no one else would think of.
I physically take it apart and mess around with the pieces until I force a solution.
I sit back, do the logical steps in my head, and mentally solve it before even touching it.

questions.scenario: Which of these science news headlines would make you click immediately?

options.text: 'New Earth-like Exoplanet Discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope!'
'Scientists Achieve Quantum Teleportation of Information Over 100 Miles!'
'CERN's Large Hadron Collider Upgraded to Smash Particles Harder Than Ever!'
'New Mathematical Equation Might Finally Link Gravity with Quantum Mechanics!'

questions.scenario: If you could pick your dream workspace, what would it look like?

options.text: A quiet, massive observatory sitting at the top of a remote mountain, away from city lights.
A sterile, ultra-cold laboratory working with lasers and experimental quantum computers.
A giant underground facility filled with cables, magnets, heavy machinery, and control rooms.
A quiet, cozy office with a giant chalkboard, a pile of notebooks, and a cup of coffee.

questions.scenario: In a group debate with your friends, what is your arguing style?

options.text: I make everyone zoom out and look at the grand scheme of things so they stop arguing over small details.
I bring up paradoxes and weird 'what if' scenarios that make everyone question reality.
I demand actual physical proof or a live demonstration before I believe anything they say.
I use pure, step-by-step logic and mathematical reasoning to completely dismantle their argument.

questions.scenario: If you were remembered in history for discovering one thing, what would it be?

options.text: Discovering undeniable proof of alien life or the exact origin of the universe.
Inventing a perfectly functioning, instant teleportation device.
Discovering a brand-new, unseen physical particle using a massive machine.
Writing the 'Theory of Everything'—a single, elegant equation that explains the entire universe.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video are you most likely to watch at 2 AM?

options.text: A documentary showing the true scale of the universe, black holes, and distant galaxies.
A video explaining the double-slit experiment, Schrödinger's cat, and quantum entanglement.
Videos of people smashing things in extreme slow motion or building crazy engineering gadgets.
A math genius solving impossible equations or explaining what the 4th dimension looks like.

Astrophysicist.title: Astrophysicist / Cosmologist
Astrophysicist.primary_match_text: You are fascinated by the big picture and the grand scale of the universe. You want to understand stars, galaxies, black holes, and the origins of everything.
Astrophysicist.day_in_the_life: Analyzing data from deep-space telescopes, mapping out distant galaxies, and trying to understand the behavior of massive stars and dark matter.
Astrophysicist.alternative_match_text: Because you love studying space and big data, working in aerospace or satellite communications is a great alternative career.
Astrophysicist.roadmap: Take PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Math) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc. in Physics or Astronomy, followed by a Master's and Ph.D. in Astrophysics.

Quantum_Physicist.title: Quantum Physicist
Quantum_Physicist.primary_match_text: You are drawn to the bizarre and the impossible. You love the microscopic world where the normal rules of physics break down, and reality becomes strange and fascinating.
Quantum_Physicist.day_in_the_life: Working with incredibly cold temperatures and lasers to study subatomic particles, or developing the next generation of super-powerful quantum computers.
Quantum_Physicist.alternative_match_text: If you love cutting-edge tech and quantum rules, working in advanced materials science or nanotechnology is a highly lucrative backup plan.
Quantum_Physicist.roadmap: Take PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc. in Physics, then specialize with a Master's and Ph.D. in Quantum Mechanics or Condensed Matter Physics.

Experimental_Physicist.title: Experimental Physicist
Experimental_Physicist.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on builder. You don't just want to do math on a board; you want to build massive machines, smash particles together, and test theories in the real world.
Experimental_Physicist.day_in_the_life: Designing massive particle accelerators, firing high-energy lasers, and running complex physical experiments to prove or disprove scientific theories.
Experimental_Physicist.alternative_match_text: Since you love building complex machines and running physical tests, becoming an Electronics or Mechanical Engineer is a fantastic alternative.
Experimental_Physicist.roadmap: Take PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Engineering Physics or a B.Sc. in Physics, focusing on experimental lab work, followed by a Master's.

Theoretical_Physicist.title: Theoretical Physicist
Theoretical_Physicist.primary_match_text: You are a deep thinker and a logic master. You love using pure mathematics and mental modeling to solve the deepest mysteries of the universe without ever needing a laboratory.
Theoretical_Physicist.day_in_the_life: Sitting with a chalkboard and a computer, writing complex mathematical equations to explain gravity, string theory, or multiple dimensions.
Theoretical_Physicist.alternative_match_text: With your incredible math and logic skills, working as an Applied Mathematician, Data Scientist, or Cryptographer are high-paying alternatives.
Theoretical_Physicist.roadmap: Take PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc. in Mathematics or Physics, with a strong focus on advanced calculus, followed by a Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics.
